subject: Interim sovereignty acknowledgement and transient sync window request
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@blueharborhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data locality — processing boundary and temporary sync windows

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, security has a few hard asks on data locality we need to lock down before legal will sign the DPA:

- We need an explicit commitment that customer data that originates from EU accounts is processed and stored within EU regions by default.
- We understand failover is necessary — can you describe a "transient sync" model (maximum time window, notification process, and telemetry) if cross-region processing occurs for HA or maintenance?
- Please list subprocessors that could be involved in any transient hop (e.g., cache/CDN, telemetry, KMS). We need vendor names and region locations.
- For any transient egress > 24 hours we require prior notification and approval from our security team.

Can you send a short operational proposal that we can attach to our DPA addendum request? Ive attached a short Annex B template with the items that legal needs filled in.

Appreciate it,
Emma
Security Engineer
BlueHarbor Health
Attachment: BHH_DPA_AnnexB_Request.pdf

Subject: Re: Data locality — processing boundary and temporary sync windows

Emma,

Thanks for the clear asks and the Annex B template — forwarding to ops and legal for a consolidated response. Quick heads-up on what we expect to propose:

- Default: EU-at-rest + EU-processing for all customer data tied to EU tenants. That includes embeddings and generation token data by default.
- Transient sync model: we support short-duration cross-region processing for failover and certain operational tasks. Our standard operational commitment is to keep transients under 48 hours and to notify security within 1 hour of detection.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a roster (names and regions) but at a high level this includes: our managed GPU pools (hosted on partner cloud regions), CDN/cache providers for prefix caching, and our telemetry pipeline. KMS can be EU-hosted or customer BYOK in an EU KMS where available.

See attached draft operational summary I pushed together (redwood_region_handshake_v1.pdf). Karthik, can you add the technical notes about KV cache behavior and expected windows? Marissa, please advise on the DPA wording around "transient" vs "temporary" and approval language.

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Data locality — processing boundary and temporary sync windows

Redirecting the technical details here so the customer has a clear picture:

Emma / BlueHarbor team,

Operational constraints and what we can commit to today:

- EU-default processing: All incoming requests from EU tenants will be routed to EU-hosted model replicas and their token traces will be stored in EU-region storage.
- Short-lived transients: Two main causes for cross-region processing are (1) cold cache priming for new model weights and (2) failover when EU capacity is exhausted. For cold-cache priming we may fetch from an adjacent region for at most a few minutes per request; those traces are immediately purged from non-EU storage after cache population.
- Failover windows: We currently operate with a configurable failover window. Standard config we suggest is 48 hours for automated failover scenarios. We can support 72 hours only with explicit security/exec approval and an operational mitigation plan (accelerated purge, increased telemetry, and a post-incident evidence package).
- Subprocessors (examples):
  - Managed GPU provider: PartnerCloud EU-west1 (compute)
  - CDN / Cache: FastEdge (eu-central) — used for prefix/KV caching only
  - Telemetry / metrics: TelemetryFlow (eu-west) — logs aggregated for SLOs
  - KMS: Redwood-managed EU KMS (or customer BYOK in EU)

- Notifications and evidence: We will send an automated incident-style notification to security@redwood.com and the customer-specified contact within 1 hour of a failover event. Within 72 hours we will provide an evidence package (timestamps, route maps, and attached purge logs).

Limitations / asks from BlueHarbor:
- If BlueHarbor requires a hard 0% cross-border processing SLA (i.e., no transient hops under any condition) we will need to move to a dedicated private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with capacity commitments and a different pricing profile.
- For approval of windows > 48 hours, ops needs a signed exception in the DPA addendum and a single point of contact for rapid approval.

I can produce a one-page operational playbook with exact TTLs and purge controls for the DPA annex.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure & Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@blueharborhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data locality — processing boundary and temporary sync windows

Emma — summarizing and next steps so we have alignment for legal: 

- Offer: EU-bound processing by default, with a standard transient failover allowance of up to 48 hours.
- Notifications: Redwood will notify BlueHarbor security and the customer POC within 1 hour of any transient cross-region processing event.
- Evidence: Post-event package (route maps, purge confirmations, timestamps) delivered within 72 hours.
- Subprocessors: Full roster will be included in the DPA addendum (high-level list above; full list in the Annex).
- KMS options: Redwood-managed EU KMS or customer BYOK in EU — note that BYOK requires additional onboarding steps.

If BlueHarbor accepts 48 hours as the transient window we will:
1) Populate Annex B with the operational playbook and subprocessors.
2) Circulate a DPA addendum via DocuSign (Marissa will drive the legal text).
3) Provide the one-page ops playbook from Karthik and a sample evidence package template.

Please confirm by EOD Monday if 48 hours is acceptable. If you need a stricter window (24 hours or forbidding any hops) let us know so we can outline dedicated deployment alternatives and timelines.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
